entries.api: rclcppyy.enable_cpp_acceleration() before rclpy/message imports
entries.notes: The default compatible profile preserves stock node, context, executor, message, entity, and Publisher.publish authority. Its import and activation graph excludes cppyy, Cling bringup, native factories, and the legacy node. Explicit publisher_cpp and required_cpp profiles separately expose the certified same-handle C++ publisher route.

entries.api: RCLCPPYY_ENABLE_HOOK=1 with an installed startup hook
entries.notes: A fresh interpreter proves default compatible startup activation. Node, Publisher.publish, executor, and Future behavior remains stock-authoritative and reports Python authority.

entries.api: RCLCPPYY_ENABLE_HOOK=1 with RCLCPPYY_HOOK_PROFILE=direct_cpp and optional registered interfaces/optimizations
entries.notes: The explicitly selected direct profile activates from the installed startup bootstrap before rclpy eagerly imports generated control messages. A fresh Jazzy/Cyclone process proves an unchanged user import receives the direct Node and exact generated C++ nested Header/Time classes registered through the comma-separated interface input. Entity operations retain the bounded direct_cpp fail-closed contract and never fall back through an application-message conversion or serialized route. Compatible remains the default hook profile.

entries.api: Installed startup hook with RCLCPPYY_ENABLE_HOOK unset or not 1
entries.notes: Fresh interpreters remain on unmodified stock behavior.

entries.api: enable_cpp_acceleration() after rclpy or message modules are imported
entries.notes: The original Node, Publisher, executor, LifecycleNode, ActionClient, and ActionServer classes are patched in place and message classes are not replaced. Future completion methods retain exact stock identity so executor Task completion has no instrumentation overhead. Function aliases captured from the rclpy module before activation retain stock behavior but are not instrumented; overridden subclass methods remain user-owned.

entries.api: rclpy.create_node()
entries.notes: Returns the exact stock Node. The custom Context, namespace, remaps, parameters, graph identity, and teardown are covered by the differential contract.

entries.api: rclcppyy.Node(name)
entries.notes: Direct construction and get_name are tested; broader Node behavior is covered by individual entries.

entries.api: profile=direct_cpp DirectNode context, CLI arguments, parameter overrides, and rclcpp::NodeOptions flags
entries.notes: On Jazzy/Cyclone, DirectNode lowers the active runtime context, local CLI arguments, exact direct/native Parameter overrides, use_global_arguments, enable_rosout, start_parameter_services, allow_undeclared_parameters, automatically_declare_parameters_from_overrides, and enable_logger_service to rclcpp::NodeOptions. Foreign contexts, malformed arguments, non-native overrides, and non-boolean flags reject before runtime or NativeSession node ownership changes. Live graph and parameter evidence covers local/global remaps, CLI overrides, deferred/automatic/implicit declaration, rosout, parameter services, and logger services with conversion and serialization paths poisoned.

entries.api: Node name/namespace and endpoint identity observed through the ROS graph
entries.notes: Activated and stock scenarios expose the same single requested node and endpoint identity; no companion node is created.

entries.api: profile=direct_cpp graph names/types, endpoint counts, name resolution, and wait_for_node
entries.notes: The direct Node delegates topic/service names and types, node names/namespaces/enclaves, fully-qualified node names, per-node publisher/subscriber/service/client names and types, endpoint counts, topic/service expansion and remapping, endpoint-detail queries, and wait_for_node to its exact rclcpp graph/topics/services interfaces. Native TopicEndpointInfo is shaped into the real rclpy control object with node identity, generated type hash, endpoint kind, 16-byte GID, and complete RMW QoS. Only graph metadata is materialized into documented Python return objects; application message data remains generated C++. Valid remapping, malformed-name fail-closed behavior, missing-node exception identity, four native endpoint kinds, conversion/serialization poison, and teardown pass on Jazzy/Cyclone. Graph-event waiting remains uncovered.

entries.api: Existing subclasses of a Node alias imported before activation
entries.notes: The application corpus constructs an exact pre-activation subclass, preserves its base and Context, and exercises inherited routed methods. Methods explicitly overridden by an application remain application-owned.

entries.api: Generated .msg class imported after activation
entries.notes: Generated message classes remain the original Python classes with unchanged identity and constructor behavior in compatible mode.

entries.api: profile=message_facade generated-style std_msgs/String and UInt64
entries.notes: On the reviewed Jazzy rclpy 7.1.11/Cyclone stack, late-imported String and UInt64 facades own distinct C++ messages and preserve the tested generated constructor, valid-field, repr, equality, copy, pickle, callback, MessageInfo, stock entity, graph, callback-group, destruction, and reinitialization observations. Same-handle publish and serialized take avoid Python-to-C++ whole-message conversion. Unsupported layouts, stale imports, raw/event/content-filter subscriptions, and custom publishers remain visibly stock; invalid unchecked field assignments may fail earlier to preserve valid C++ storage, and take failure propagates without an unsafe retry. No performance benefit is asserted.

entries.api: profile=direct_cpp registered installed message pub/sub slice
entries.notes: On Jazzy/Cyclone, early activation replaces the default String/UInt64 imports and explicitly registered canonical package/msg/Message interfaces with actual generated C++ classes. Installed rosidl metadata, generated headers, canonical cppyy aliases, and C++ typesupport are required; nested message dependencies are resolved before aliases change. One NativeSession owns the rclcpp node, publisher, subscription, and executor for the common subclassed Node, integer-depth entity, and spin/spin_once pattern. Publishing uses the exact C++ object. Baseline callbacks receive one owning C++ copy; the subscription_shared_lease option instead shares the received allocation with zero MessageT deep copies. One- and two-argument callback shapes expose either the message alone or that same generated C++ message plus native rclcpp MessageInfo fields. All routes poison and avoid generated-Python conversion and serialization, retain callback values safely, and support native callback groups and the direct public single-threaded executor. Python message classes, stale imports, missing interfaces, unsupported QoS/options, and uncovered operations fail closed. Five clean x86-64 Jazzy/Cyclone characterization runs cover flat String and nested Header at 1 and 10 kHz with verified C++ markers and no case failures; direct combined CPU is substantially below stock, while the lease has no consistent CPU advantage over the C++ copy. A ten-repetition MessageInfo relay characterization records 0.190x stock-info relay CPU and 0.288x combined CPU with zero conversions or serialization calls. The incomplete surface remains experimental, and raw shared-host artifacts are descriptive rather than release claims.

entries.api: Nested messages and primitive sequences on the unpatched-message native rclcpp path
entries.notes: The reusable native path has recursive conversion and sequence coverage; transparent import-hook identity for these shapes is not implied.

entries.api: Generated service and action class import redirection
entries.notes: Compatible mode does not redirect generated imports. One source-built nested message/service/action package is proven with stock generated classes and behavior, but broader generated interface shapes are not implied.

entries.api: Node.create_publisher(message_type, topic, depth_or_qos)
entries.notes: Creation, QoS ownership, graph endpoint, destruction, and default compatible publishing remain stock-authoritative. publisher_cpp and required_cpp explicitly select C++ serialization over the same native handle and complete ordered round trips. Private Node-constructor infrastructure is excluded from route preparation. No performance benefit is asserted.

entries.api: Node's private parameter-event publisher construction
entries.notes: Node construction creates its private publisher entirely through stock rclpy under compatible, required-C++, and optimized policies. A deterministic required-C++ probe proves same-handle route preparation is not invoked for this infrastructure and is invoked exactly once for the following explicit publisher.

entries.api: Publisher callback_group, event_callbacks, qos_overriding_options, and publisher_class
entries.notes: Exact stock construction preserves a custom publisher class, callback-group membership, complete endpoint QoS, and non-empty depth/reliability overrides. Live incompatible-QoS and matched user callbacks match stock; the reviewed upstream event contract also covers deadline/liveliness callback construction and event-handle lifetime. Middleware- and type-specific event generation outside that matrix is not implied.

entries.api: Node.create_subscription(message_type, topic, callback, depth_or_qos)
entries.notes: The complete subscription entity and Python callback dispatch remain stock; ordered delivery and visible backend fallback are covered.

entries.api: Subscription callback_group, event_callbacks, qos_overriding_options, raw mode, and content filters
entries.notes: Exact stock construction preserves callback groups, complete endpoint QoS, non-empty depth/reliability overrides, serialized raw delivery, and live incompatible-QoS and matched callbacks. The no-skip Fast DDS gate certifies all 21 reviewed subscription tests, including content-filter create/set/get/reset/effect; the same six tests remain legitimate skips on Cyclone DDS, which does not provide that feature. Message-lost and type-incompatibility triggers outside the reviewed event matrix are not implied.

entries.api: Node.create_timer(period, Python callback)
entries.notes: Stock timer authority is explicit. The corpus covers callback groups, autostart=false, reset, callback execution, cancellation, exception propagation, and destruction; required_cpp rejects before creation.

entries.api: profile=direct_cpp Node.create_timer including inspection, autostart=False, cancel/reset/destroy, spin, and spin_once
entries.notes: On Jazzy/Cyclone, the opt-in profile creates a real rclcpp WallTimer on the NativeSession executor and enters the Python callback once per firing without message conversion, serialization, or a per-firing data copy. is_ready delegates to TimerBase::is_ready, time_until_next_call uses TimerBase::time_until_trigger and maps the canceled nanoseconds-max sentinel to None, and time_since_last_call reads rcl_timer_get_time_since_last_call from the exact native handle. Pre-fire, post-fire, canceled, reset, destroyed-handle, and stable timer_period_ns behavior pass with conversion and serialization poisoned. Default clock, callback groups, continuous periodic use, and native autostart=false construction followed by reset are covered; custom clocks and unsupported options fail before entity creation. Controlled evidence shows substantially lower process CPU and better consecutive-interval jitter than stock, but materially worse first-reset error and absolute scheduled phase. The route remains experimental and is not suitable for reset-sensitive deadlines.

entries.api: rclpy.spin(accelerated_node)
entries.notes: The stock executor remains authoritative and is reported as Python. Compatible and required-C++ preserve their existing behavior. The explicit optimized profile bounds each stock wait to 100 ms; fresh-process immediate-SIGTERM tests cover global spin without claiming a performance benefit.

entries.api: rclpy.spin_once(accelerated_node, timeout_sec=...)
entries.notes: The wrapper delegates to stock execution and reports Python authority. Timer, guard, service, simulated-time, custom executor, signature, and required_cpp fail-before-spin behavior are covered. Timer, subscription, service, and guard callback exceptions preserve their exact user-defined Python types.

entries.api: profile=direct_cpp Executor/SingleThreadedExecutor ownership and top-level spin APIs
entries.notes: On Jazzy/Cyclone, direct nodes start unowned and can be added, removed, or transferred between public SingleThreadedExecutor facades backed by exact rclcpp executors. Top-level spin, spin_once, spin_until_future_complete, blocked-wait wake, context-manager shutdown, callback exceptions, node destruction, and generated-C++ pub/sub and Future completion are covered. Repeated global spin_once retains native membership without exposing logical membership, avoiding per-call executor guard churn. The corrected ten-repetition characterization records 0.260x stock CPU for explicit ownership and 0.322x for the source-compatible global route, but the explicit facade remains 1.279x its raw rclcpp control and therefore has no raw-parity claim. MultiThreadedExecutor and create_task fail closed.

entries.api: profile=direct_cpp default, mutually-exclusive, and reentrant native callback groups
entries.notes: The direct Node exposes its real rclcpp default group and lazily binds explicit mutually-exclusive or reentrant facades to their first native node. Publishers, subscriptions including lease and MessageInfo routes, timers, services, clients, and action clients pass the exact native group through rclcpp options or overloads. Cross-node reuse fails before entity creation and group/entity lifetimes are retained through teardown. Single-threaded execution is covered; concurrent callback-group behavior remains unclaimed while MultiThreadedExecutor is fail-closed.

entries.api: MultiThreadedExecutor with reentrant and mutually exclusive callback groups
entries.notes: A two-thread MultiThreadedExecutor with a reentrant callback group, shutdown, status reporting, exception preservation, and required_cpp rejection is covered by differential evidence. The stock executor remains authoritative; custom Executor subclasses and sustained cross-architecture stress are not implied.

entries.api: Custom Executor subclasses, overridden scheduling internals, and sustained cross-architecture stress
entries.notes: Selected stock executor extensions are covered separately. Arbitrary Executor overrides can bypass or conflict with patched methods, and sustained workload evidence across architectures remains incomplete.

entries.api: profile=optimized bounded rclpy and stock executor spin waits
entries.notes: Fifteen fresh x86-64 processes receive SIGTERM immediately from an active callback across global, direct single-threaded, and direct multi-threaded spin; all exit cleanly and prove structured policy, signature, and ownership invariants. The 100 ms bound adds periodic idle wake-ups. ARM64 and sustained middleware-matrix evidence remain required before promotion.

entries.api: rclpy.task.Future set_result/set_exception/cancel completion
entries.notes: Future completion remains stock-authoritative under every policy to avoid destabilizing executor internals and per-callback overhead. Fresh-process tests prove exact stock set_result, set_exception, and cancel method identity for compatible, publisher_cpp, required_cpp, and optimized profiles; behavioral parity covers results, exceptions, cancellation, and done callbacks.

entries.api: Node.create_guard_condition/GuardCondition.trigger/destroy_guard_condition
entries.notes: Stock guard-condition identity, callback groups, trigger/dispatch, destruction, compatible status, bounded warnings, signature preservation, and required_cpp rejection before creation are covered.

entries.api: Node.create_service/create_client and service spinning
entries.notes: A local SetBool client/server request, Future response, callback group, discovery, status, identity, and teardown match stock. required_cpp rejects user service/client creation before side effects while preserving constructor-owned services.

entries.api: profile=direct_cpp registered installed service create_service/create_client, call_async, and spin_until_future_complete
entries.notes: On Jazzy/Cyclone, early activation replaces the default SetBool and explicitly registered canonical package/srv/Service Request and Response aliases with actual generated C++ classes and creates real rclcpp service/client entities. Installed services and nested message dependencies are resolved before transactional alias mutation; missing, stale, and unregistered types fail before graph creation. The common synchronous two-argument callback, call_async/Future, and stock-shaped blocking call with a servicing executor on another thread work with default service QoS: callback requests are owning C++ copies, responses are assigned in C++, client requests make one native C++ value copy, and returned results remain C++. There is no Python-message conversion or serialization bridge. Each operation uses an unmodified stock rclpy.task.Future only as Python control state; no global Future method is patched. Blocking call timeout removes the native pending request, and callback use retains the stock deadlock warning. Custom QoS/groups, coroutine callbacks, introspection, and manual response send fail closed. SetBool plus explicitly registered Trigger are covered by stock and compiled rclcpp peers in both directions, cancellation, timeouts, exceptions, retained values, status authority, teardown, and reinitialization. A clean five-repetition x86-64 Trigger client characterization records median paired direct/stock ratios of 0.218x CPU, 0.373x p50, 0.429x p99, and 2.634x throughput with exact C++ and no-conversion markers. The bounded surface remains experimental pending broader service API coverage, dedicated-host thresholds, and ARM64 measurement.

entries.api: profile=direct_cpp LookupTransform ActionClient async goal, feedback, result, and cancel slice
entries.notes: On Jazzy/Cyclone, early direct_cpp activation keeps the default tf2_msgs/action/LookupTransform client and accepts explicitly registered canonical installed actions. Goal, Feedback, Result, UUID, SendGoal/GetResult request and response, feedback-message, CancelGoal request and response, and nested payload aliases are validated transactionally and replaced with their actual generated C++ classes. A custom nested Accumulate action passes fresh-cache interoperability against a compiled rclcpp_action server, retains C++ values after teardown, and links its installed typesupport with an explicit RUNPATH. A real rclcpp_action client and batched C++ readiness snapshot drive send_goal_async, feedback callbacks, get_result_async, and cancel_goal_async without generated-Python message conversion or serialization. Goal acceptance/rejection, exactly ordered feedback, success, cancellation, retained values, graph identity, callback exceptions, endpoint loss, teardown, and reinitialization are covered. Missing, stale, and unregistered actions fail before graph creation; custom goal UUIDs, non-default action QoS, synchronous calls, introspection, and uncovered options remain fail-closed. A clean five-repetition x86-64 LookupTransform characterization after generic registration records median paired direct/stock ratios of 0.231x CPU, 0.833x accept p50, 0.314x accept p99, 0.986x result p50, 0.960x result p99, and 1.016x throughput with exact C++ authority, no conversion, no feedback drops, and clean teardown. This remains a bounded experimental client slice pending broader action-client API coverage, dedicated-host thresholds, a custom-action performance workload, and ARM64 measurement.

entries.api: profile=direct_cpp ActionServer synchronous goal/cancel/accepted/execute callbacks, feedback, result, and cancellation slice
entries.notes: On Jazzy/Cyclone, the direct ActionServer keeps Goal, Feedback, Result, UUID, action envelopes, accepted-goal state, and rclcpp_action server authority in C++. Synchronous Python callbacks receive the exact generated C++ values; converters and serializers are poisoned in the live proof. Server-first executor polling covers acceptance, staged feedback, success, rejection, cancellation, default abort, callback errors, deferred accepted goals, retained values, safe deferred server close, teardown, and reinitialization. Node or context teardown attempted inside an active server callback fails before mutation. This P0 slice requires the single-threaded executor, a mutually-exclusive callback group, default action QoS, and synchronous callbacks; concurrency, coroutine callbacks, custom QoS, introspection, and uncovered options fail closed. No stock/direct CPU comparison exists yet, so this entry is implementation coverage only and carries no performance claim.

entries.api: ActionClient and ActionServer with generated action types: accept, reject, feedback, result, and cancel
entries.notes: Exact stock ActionClient/ActionServer objects, generated types, nodes, custom Context, reentrant groups, and MultiThreadedExecutor semantics remain authoritative. Activated behavior must equal stock for success, rejection, complete feedback, result, cancellation, callback order, and teardown; status reports Python ownership and required_cpp rejects before handle or waitable creation. No C++ action route is claimed.

entries.api: Stock-authoritative Python ActionClient interoperating with an ahead-of-time rclcpp_action server
entries.notes: A generated nested action proves discovery, goal acceptance, feedback, successful result, and teardown against a separately compiled C++ server on local x86-64. The same source proof is wired into native ARM64 CI but is not certified there until a remote run succeeds. The Python client remains explicitly reported as Python-owned.

entries.api: Concurrent goals, abort, execute exceptions, feedback validation, cancellation, and result expiry
entries.notes: The pinned activated upstream ActionServer contract covers multiple and duplicate goals, accept/reject, abort, execute exceptions, feedback type errors, cancellation, and result expiry. These paths remain exact stock rclpy behavior; no C++ action route is claimed.

entries.api: Custom action QoS, explicit goal UUIDs, and synchronous action client and goal-handle calls
entries.notes: The generated-action differential constructs an ActionClient with custom goal, result, and cancel service QoS plus custom feedback and status subscription QoS; injects and observes a fixed goal UUID; and exercises Jazzy's public synchronous ActionClient.send_goal(), ClientGoalHandle.cancel_goal(), and ClientGoalHandle.get_result() methods under a servicing executor. Results, cancellation, teardown, and the complete recorded contract match stock on local x86-64. Jazzy has no public ActionClient-level synchronous cancel or result method, so none is claimed. The same source proof is wired into native ARM64 CI but is not certified there until a remote run succeeds.

entries.api: Local parameter declaration, callbacks, mutation, listing, and parameter-service graph
entries.notes: The stock node remains sole owner. Values, overrides, callbacks, mutation, listing, service graph identity, status, custom Context, and required_cpp rejection before mutation are covered.

entries.api: profile=direct_cpp owning Parameter facade plus local declare/get/type/set/atomic/describe/list and pre/on/post callbacks
entries.notes: On Jazzy/Cyclone, each rclpy-shaped Parameter facade owns one rclcpp::Parameter and local DirectNode parameter operations retain native rclcpp node authority. Parameter, ParameterValue, ParameterDescriptor, range, ListParametersResult, and SetParametersResult imports are actual generated C++ aliases; non-C++ control messages, descriptors, and callback results fail before mutation. Python values are materialized only by the explicit .value property. All ten parameter kinds, empty typed arrays, native pre/on/post callbacks, rejection, callback errors, retained lifetime, teardown, and reinitialization pass with converter, serializer, and CDR tripwires at zero. Exact direct/native constructor overrides and the undeclared/automatic-declaration policies are covered by node.direct_cpp_options. Undeclare, descriptor mutation, parameter-event observation, and remote clients remain uncovered or fail closed. The CPU-first stock/direct/raw benchmark harness covers declare, native-object get, explicit value snapshot, and atomic set, but only its bounded smoke has run; no performance claim exists until the repeated characterization is reviewed.

entries.api: AsyncParameterClient and remote parameter events
entries.notes: An AsyncParameterClient discovers all six stock services, remotely sets and gets a declared parameter, observes the matching ParameterEvent value, and tears down every client and subscription. The exact stock objects remain authoritative and activated behavior matches the stock corpus.

entries.api: LifecycleNode construction, configure, cleanup, and unconfigured shutdown
entries.notes: The exact stock class, pre-activation subclass, Context, state machine, callbacks, and teardown remain authoritative. Communication-enabled and disabled construction, successful and failed configure callbacks, cleanup, unconfigured shutdown, bounded fallback reporting, signature preservation, and required_cpp rejection before Node initialization are covered.

entries.api: LifecycleNode change_state, get_state, get_available_states, get_available_transitions, and get_transition_graph services
entries.notes: All five stock lifecycle services are discovered and queried in a custom Context. Service-driven activate/deactivate, state responses, transition inventories, callback inputs, and client teardown match the stock application corpus; lifecycle-node status represents their aggregate stock ownership.

entries.api: LifecycleNode.create_lifecycle_publisher and activation-gated publish
entries.notes: The exact stock LifecyclePublisher, managed activation flag, and publish operation remain authoritative in compatible mode. Inactive publishes are suppressed; active delivery, deactivation, and destruction match stock.

entries.api: LifecycleNode ERROR callback processing, invalid transitions, and shutdown from active or inactive states
entries.notes: The isolated CycloneDDS differential covers explicit ERROR returns and raised configure exceptions, on_error callback order and recovery to unconfigured, RCLError type and stable message parity for invalid activate, deactivate, cleanup, and finalized shutdown transitions, and successful shutdown callbacks from inactive and active states. The exact stock LifecycleNode remains authoritative and the complete observations match stock.

entries.api: Normal interpreter exit after rclcpp bringup and node creation
entries.notes: Both the native lane and compatible stock-authority scenario return normally without forced exit, leaked graph identity, or teardown fault.

entries.api: Repeated explicit Context init/shutdown cycles while another Context exists
entries.notes: Three sequential custom Contexts each create exact stock entities, complete a stock-authoritative round trip, tear down, and leave the default Context untouched while the corpus Context remains live.

entries.api: Repeated init/shutdown of the default global Context
entries.notes: Compatible mode supports repeated default-global init/shutdown with stock authority. An isolated Jazzy/CycloneDDS regression adds the stronger proof of three sequential default-global init, same-handle C++ publish, spin, full entity teardown, and shutdown cycles under the explicit publisher_cpp profile.

entries.api: C++ message CDR serialization compared with rclpy.serialization
entries.notes: Flat and tested message bytes match the stock serializer; this is a native capability and not yet a global rclpy.serialization patch.

entries.api: get_action_names_and_types and per-node action client/server graph queries
entries.notes: The pinned activated action-graph tests preserve names, types, and node identity. These graph queries are untouched stock rclpy operations.

entries.api: Stock Context construction, init/shutdown sequences, signals, domain IDs, callbacks, and context-manager use
entries.notes: The selected initialization and Context files pass with compatible activation, including invalid sequences and repeated shutdown. The separate repeated-default entry covers explicit same-handle C++ publishing between default Context cycles.

entries.api: Callback groups, add/remove node, tasks and coroutines, spin_until_future_complete, selected Waitables, and EventsExecutor
entries.notes: The pinned activated tests cover stock single- and multi-threaded scheduling, tasks, coroutine callbacks, runtime entity mutation, callback-group exclusion, representative custom waitables, and the opt-in EventsExecutor. EventsExecutor retains its upstream experimental status; arbitrary Executor method overrides and sustained stress are excluded from this entry.

entries.api: Topic expansion and validation, namespace/node validation, hidden-name classification, TopicEndpointInfo, and TypeHash graph values
entries.notes: The pinned value and validation tests preserve accepted values, invalid indices, exception types, endpoint identity, GIDs, QoS, and type hashes.

entries.api: Logger hierarchy, severity, throttling, rosout transport, and logging services
entries.notes: Activated upstream tests cover logger configuration and formatting, once/throttle/skip-first filters, ROS-time throttling, rosout delivery and disablement, hierarchy, and get/set logging services.

entries.api: Generated Python message defaults, constants, equality, inequality, and serialization errors
entries.notes: Compatible activation retains the installed generated Python classes, and the selected message tests preserve their value semantics. Arbitrary interface shapes beyond the reviewed generated packages are not implied.

entries.api: Stock Node accessors, graph queries/counts, name resolution, clocks, logger, executor association, parameter files, dynamic entity creation, and destruction
entries.notes: The full selected Node, create-while-spinning, and destruction files pass under activation. This entry covers unchanged stock behavior, including invalid-handle and active-executor teardown, but excludes private native-handle mutation.

entries.api: Parameter values and conversion, YAML parsing, descriptors, and ParameterEventHandler callback management
entries.notes: The selected parameter value and event-handler tests preserve arrays, equality, validation, YAML loading, callback registration/removal/order, event matching, and path resolution.

entries.api: QoS profiles, policies, presets, compatibility, events, and overriding options
entries.notes: Construction, conversion, validation, compatibility, runtime overrides, event-handle lifetime, incompatible-QoS callbacks, and matched/unmatched callbacks remain stock-authoritative. Middleware-specific event generation outside the reviewed matrix is not implied.

entries.api: rclpy.serialization.serialize_message and deserialize_message
entries.notes: Stock serialization round trips and error behavior pass under activation. The separate native CDR API is opt-in and does not replace these functions.

entries.api: Client synchronous/asynchronous calls, concurrency, discovery, remapping, timeouts, and service introspection
entries.notes: The pinned activated tests cover concurrent and synchronous calls, timeout behavior, name remapping, type rejection, timestamps, and service-introspection metadata and contents. No C++ service route is claimed.

entries.api: rclpy.wait_for_message with default or explicit QoS and timeout
entries.notes: The synchronous convenience API remains stock-authoritative and passes message, explicit-QoS, and timeout cases under activation.

entries.api: Clock, ROSClock, Time, Duration, Rate, TimeSource, jump callbacks, sleep, and simulated time
entries.notes: The selected tests cover construction, arithmetic and comparison, message conversion, clock sleep and shutdown, ROS-time activation, jumps, clock attachment, Rate destruction/wake, and /clock delivery.

entries.api: TypeHash values and type-support checks for installed generated message and service classes
entries.notes: TypeHash semantics and happy-path type-support loading used by selected waitables are covered. Negative checks requiring the upstream-built test extension are tracked separately as unassessed.

entries.api: Default-context helpers, ROS argument removal, ok/shutdown helpers, RMW identity, available RMWs, timeout conversion, and signal options
entries.notes: The pinned utilities and initialization tests preserve process helper return values and signal-handler option behavior. Default-Context reuse after C++ bringup remains subject to the explicit unsupported entry.

entries.api: Destruction ordering after direct mutation of the private native context_handle
entries.notes: The unchanged pinned test fails with the stock installed extension because its ad hoc private context_handle assignment is rejected. Normal public destruction behavior is covered separately; this private mutation is not compatibility evidence.

entries.api: TypeDescriptionService request using a graph-derived TypeHash
entries.notes: The unchanged pinned test fails with stock rclpy 7.1.11 because the installed client rejects the graph-derived TypeHash. The source-only gate therefore cannot establish backend compatibility for this request path.

entries.api: Type-support validation failures for invalid message, service, and mock types
entries.notes: The excluded test requires the upstream repository's separately built test extension. Installed generated types are covered on the happy path, but these negative and mock-type contracts remain unassessed.
